title: CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE. On prayer: definition
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): It stands as also called invocation or adoration; metaphorically sacrifice, incense, calves belonging toward ye lips. In ye regenerate it stands as nearly a compendium belonging toward all good works. — Prayer stands as an exercise belonging toward piety and Christian warfare by which believers, at ye Spirit's impulse and in Jesus Christ's name, address God ye Father by petition and thanksgiving concerning goods toward be given or already given, and evils toward be averted or already averted. — CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE. On prayer.
pass_b_english: Prayer is an exercise of piety and Christian warfare by which believers, at the Spirit's impulse and in Jesus Christ's name, address God the Father by petition and thanksgiving concerning goods to be given or already given, and evils to be averted or already averted.
It is also called invocation or adoration; metaphorically sacrifice, incense, calves of the lips. In the regenerate it is nearly a compendium of all good works.
source_text: CAPUT VIGESIMUM PRIMUM, De precatione. Precatio est exercitium pietatis et militiae Christianae, quo fideles Deum Patrem de bonis dandis aut datis, malisque averruncandis aut averruncatis, impulsu Spiritus Sancti in nomine Iesu Christi petendo et gratias agendo compellant. Alias invocatio, alias adoratio dicitur. Per metaphoram sacrificium, suffimentum, vituli labiorum (Heb. 13:15). Est complexus et compendium fere omnium bonorum operum in homine renato.
